title: Automotive CRM pricing: compare the full cost, not just the subscription
summary: Compare automotive CRM pricing with a fill-in worksheet covering subscriptions, usage, integrations, migration, training, contract terms and retained tools.
body_markdown:
Automotive CRM pricing depends on the package your dealership buys: stores and users, communication volume, AI modules, integrations, implementation and contract terms. A monthly subscription alone does not tell you what it will cost to run the required workflow.


The official automotive CRM pages reviewed for this guide did not establish comparable dollar prices for complete dealership packages. Get written quotes for the same scope, then use the[downloadable CRM quote worksheet](https://www.useclearline.com/resources/automotive-crm-quote-worksheet.md) to compare them. It is deliberately unfilled: add approved vendor quotes and your store’s costs rather than treating example numbers as a budget.


This guide is about the customer workspace and its operating dependencies. For the cost of phone coverage and follow-up, use the separate[AI BDC pricing guide](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/ai-bdc-pricing-dealerships) . The[dealership AI buying hub](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/pillars/dealership-ai-buying-guide) connects both evaluations.


## What the current public sources tell you


Reviewed **October 26, 2026** . “Amount not established” means no comparable amount was verified from the reviewed page. It does not mean a vendor has no price list elsewhere, every package is negotiated, or an older third-party estimate is current.

Use the[automotive CRM shortlist](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/best-automotive-crm-software) to decide which products deserve that work.


## The six cost categories to put in every CRM quote


### 1. Store, user and module fees


Record the base fee, number of rooftops, included users, extra-user rate and any minimum commitment. Name every selected module: CRM, AI response, voice, marketing, desking or another retail product.


Ask whether managers, service staff, administrators and inactive accounts count toward licensing. If a quote is group-wide, identify the fee for adding another store and which functions are shared.


### 2. Communication and AI usage


Write down the billing unit before estimating volume. It might be a call, minute, message, active contact or another unit. Confirm included volume, overages, minimums and how short calls, transfers or failed messages are counted.


Keep voice, SMS, email, phone numbers and AI modules separate unless the quote explicitly bundles them. Price expected usage and a busier month using your own history. A busy-month scenario is a planning assumption, not a vendor performance prediction.


### 3. Integrations and data access


List each required DMS, retained CRM, inventory feed, calendar, OEM lead source and phone connection. Identify vendor charges, third-party charges and any setup work separately.


The connection must also support the action you need. For example, our[PBS integration](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/clearline-pbs-systems-integration) distinguishes supported two-way contacts, vehicles and service appointments from pull-only Workplan records. A fee for a connection does not imply every record can be updated in both directions.


### 4. Implementation, migration and training


Scope the data objects, historical depth, field mapping, duplicate handling, staff ownership and training. Ask which work the vendor performs, which the dealership performs and what requires another provider.


Contact import is one task. Moving opportunity stages, active follow-up, appointment history, attachments and audit records may require different work. Confirm those objects individually before using “migration included” in the budget.


### 5. Tools retained during and after the change


Include temporary overlap with the current CRM and subscriptions that will remain. A new workspace may still need the DMS, desking, an equity product, a phone provider or a marketing service.


Count a subscription saving only when the store can actually end that subscription and still complete its required work. Do not subtract a tool merely because the new vendor lists a similarly named feature.


### 6. Contract, support and exit costs


Record term length, renewal date, cancellation notice, billing start, taxes, currency, support scope, renewal changes and export charges. Ask what happens to phone numbers, message history, files and connected records when the agreement ends.


Include any known remaining commitment on the old agreement. Keep unresolved terms visible rather than converting a missing price into zero.


## Give vendors one scope sheet


Send the same requirements to each shortlisted vendor:


Input What the dealership should provide


Stores and departments Rooftops, sales/service/BDC scope, shared versus store-specific processes


Users Current and planned users by role


Workflows Lead intake, opportunity ownership, tasks, conversations, booking and exceptions


Usage Recent monthly calls, minutes, messages and contacts, with a busy-month case


Systems Current DMS, CRM, inventory, calendars, phone service and lead sources


Migration Objects, history, custom fields, ownership and active campaigns to preserve


Acceptance A completed customer journey plus a failed-action and human-handoff test


Commercial terms Currency, taxes, contract period, implementation timing and export requirements


Attach the[CRM quote worksheet](https://www.useclearline.com/resources/automotive-crm-quote-worksheet.md) . Ask the vendor to label each line included, separately charged, not required or unresolved, with a quote date and reference. An unresolved integration or missing usage rate can materially change the comparison.


## Calculate first-year and ongoing cost separately


For each option, use:


**First-year cost = recurring fees during year one + expected usage and third-party costs + one-time implementation/migration/training + temporary overlap and exit costs.**


**Ongoing annual cost = recurring fees + expected usage + retained third-party costs for a full operating year.**


Use the quote’s actual billing periods. Do not multiply an annual fee by twelve or charge a one-time fee every month. Put taxes and currency conversion on their own lines if they apply.


Then identify costs that remain uncertain. If SMS overages or a DMS feed fee are missing, the first-year total is incomplete. Request the rate instead of presenting the known subtotal as the final cost.


## Assess the value with dealership outcomes


A CRM can be inexpensive and still leave opportunities without an owner. A larger package can cost more without solving the store’s main problem. Compare the cost with an agreed operating change.


Useful measures include:


- opportunities with a named owner and a dated next action;
- overdue tasks and failed handoffs resolved;
- time spent maintaining records and chasing updates;
- attended appointments by source and department;
- sales or completed repair orders linked to the workflow, where data is available.


Time released for staff is useful capacity. It becomes a cash saving only when an actual expense falls. Booked appointments are pipeline, not profit. Attribute incremental gross profit only after checking attendance, sale/RO completion, margin, cancellations and other campaigns that could explain the result.

## Frequently asked questions


How much does automotive CRM software cost? +


The reviewed official pages do not establish one comparable dealership price. Get matching quotes for stores, users, modules, usage, integrations, implementation and contract terms. Compare first-year and ongoing cost separately.


Are AI features included in dealership CRM pricing? +


That depends on the product and selected package. Some official pages list AI or surrounding products separately. Require the quote to name each included module and usage allowance.


What costs are easiest to overlook? +


Ask specifically about overages, third-party data connections, migration work, training, temporary subscription overlap, renewal terms and exports. Missing terms are unresolved inputs, not zero-cost items.


Should a dealer choose the lowest monthly price? +


Only after confirming that the package completes the required workflow. Compare full operating cost, staff adoption, integration depth and verified outcomes alongside the subscription.


Can I use the worksheet without buying from you? +


Yes. Fill it with current written quotes and your dealership’s inputs. It is a buying tool for comparing scope and cost across vendors.
